title: Division Expressions with Fractions and Whole Numbers
objective: I can explain what dividing with a whole number and a unit fraction means — how many groups fit, or how much is in one group — find the quotient with a model, and check it by multiplying.
model: tape diagram / fraction bar cut into equal pieces: how many 1/n pieces fit in a whole number, or how much is in each of n equal shares of a fraction

widgets.where: Practice §1 (items 1.1-1.4, mc/num, 1.1 carries a bar figure)
widgets.component: Sound Check: shaded fraction of a bar, fourths in a whole, 5 × 1/3, multiplication check of 12 ÷ 3
widgets.root: Prerequisite recall that matches the warm-up of the lesson; rendered the bar1 figure (3 of 8 parts shaded, key 3/8) and checked every key and distractor.

widgets.where: Practice §2 items 2.1-2.7, §3 items 3.2, 3.4, §5 items 5.4, 5.5; Challenge §5 items 5.2, 5.4 (mc/num)
widgets.component: Warm-Up Riff and Full Track word problems: meaning of 3 ÷ 1/4, expression choice, ribbon/brownie/powder/shelf/trail problems, 2/3 ÷ 4, 6 ÷ 1/5, 5 ÷ 1/4, 3/4 foot into 3, paint into 2 cans, 1/3 tube on 4 sliders
widgets.root: Every key is right, but the hints, explanations and wrong-answer feedback of 2.1 and 2.3-2.7, 3.2, 3.4, 5.4, 5.5 and challenge 5.2, 5.4 teach keep-change-flip ('put a 1 under the 4 and flip the 1/4', 'Keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, flip 2/1 to 1/2', 'multiply by the reciprocal'), the invert-and-multiply rule that 6-2 derives; this lesson is the modelling lesson (tape diagram, count the pieces, check by multiplying).
widgets.replacement: Rewrite hint ladders, x and f feedback of every listed item in model language and delete every occurrence of 'flip', 'reciprocal', 'keep, change', 'put a 1 under'. Ladder for whole ÷ unit fraction: (1) 'Name the question: how many 1/4s fit in 3?' (2) 'Each whole holds 4 fourths, so 3 wholes hold 3 × 4 fourths.' (3) 'Check: 12 × 1/4 = 3.' Ladder for fraction ÷ whole: (1) 'Share 3/4 of a pound equally in 2 kits: what is one share?' (2) 'Cut each fourth in half: the whole pound now has 8 equal pieces and one kit gets 3 of them' (3) 'Check: 3/8 × 2 = 3/4.' Key, choices and positions stay unchanged.

widgets.where: Practice §2 item 2.8 and §3 item 3.5; Challenge §2 items 2.1, 2.3, §4 items 4.1-4.3 (err)
widgets.component: Spot-the-mistake cards: '4 ÷ 3 ≈ 1.3', 'flip the first number', '1/5 of 4', 'divide straight across', 'dividing makes it smaller', 'flip the 5 to 1/5', '4/5 × 2'
widgets.root: Three of the seven (P 3.5, C 4.2, C 4.3) diagnose the flip procedure itself ('flipped the dividend', 'kept both numbers: 4/5 × 2'), and the fix and explanation text of all seven restates the rule ('dividing by a fraction is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal'). The genuine misconceptions (dividing makes numbers smaller, '1/5 of 4' for 4 ÷ 1/5, dividing numerators straight across, treating a quotient as pieces) are right for this lesson.
widgets.replacement: Keep P 2.8, C 2.1, C 2.3 and C 4.1 and rewrite their fix/x text with the model ('4 ÷ 1/3 asks how many thirds fit in 4: each foot holds 3, so 12'). Replace P 3.5, C 4.2, C 4.3 with model errors: (a) '6 ÷ 1/5: I counted 6 fifths in a foot, so 6 pieces' (counted pieces in one whole instead of 6 wholes; tap the step); (b) '3/4 ÷ 2: each share is 3/2' (multiplied; tape diagram shows a share is smaller than 3/4); (c) '5 ÷ 1/6 = 5/6 of a piece' (answered as a fraction of a piece instead of a count). Each needs three named wrong-answer feedbacks and no rule language.

widgets.component: Match whole ÷ unit fraction to quotient; match fraction ÷ whole to quotient
widgets.root: Arithmetic correct (5 ÷ 1/2 = 10 … 7 ÷ 1/2 = 14; 3/4 ÷ 2 = 3/8 … 5/8 ÷ 5 = 1/8), but hint 3 on 3.1 is 'put a 1 under the 5, flip 1/2 to 2/1' and on 3.3 'keep 3/4, change ÷ to ×, flip 2/1', and the explanations call the rule the reason.
widgets.replacement: Same pairs. Replace hints with: 3.1 'Each whole holds 2 halves; how many halves are in 5 wholes?'; 3.3 'Cut each fourth of the pound in half so the pound has 8 pieces: how many pieces does one of 2 shares get?'. Explanations count pieces and multiply to check.

widgets.component: 6 feet of tape is 1/2 of a roll (how much in the whole); 6 ÷ 1/3
widgets.root: Self-contained, right (12 feet, 18) and the stem for 3.6 states the meaning (6 ÷ 1/2 asks how much is in one whole roll); explanation text of these two does not use the rule.

widgets.component: Generated whole ÷ unit fraction expression choice with a tape diagram of the pieces
widgets.root: Rendered the tape specs over many seeds: part count = whole × denominator, total label right, expression key always whole ÷ unit fraction; also covers 'which question does a ÷ 1/n ask'.

widgets.where: Practice §4 items 4.3-4.4 (gen:fracDivWhole L2, numeric, bar figure)
widgets.component: Generated numeric whole ÷ unit fraction and unit fraction ÷ whole
widgets.root: Checked 60 seeds: answers are exact (3 ÷ 1/2 = 6, 2/3 ÷ 6 = 1/9) and the bar figure shows the dividend (n/d shaded) for the fraction ÷ whole stems.

widgets.where: Practice §4 items 4.5-4.6 and Challenge §1 items 1.3-1.4 (gen:fracDivWhole L3)
widgets.component: Generated 'which story matches', 'what does the quotient/divisor/dividend tell you', and 'which expression has the same value as 3/4 ÷ 3'
widgets.root: About one draw in four (108 of 400 seeds) is 'Which expression has the same value as a ÷ b?' with the key a × (1/b) or whole × denominator ('3/4 ÷ 3 = 3/4 × 1/3', '8 ÷ 1/4 = 8 × 4'): the multiply-by-reciprocal identity as the thing to recognise, which 6-2 derives. The story-match and role-of-each-number draws (114 of 400 and the rest) are right.
widgets.replacement: In the fracDivWhole L3 generator drop the 'same value' subtype and replace it with 'Which multiplication checks 3/4 ÷ 3 = 1/4?' (key 1/4 × 3 = 3/4; distractors 3/4 × 3, 3 × 1/4, 3/4 × 1/4) and 'How many 1/4s fit in 8? Which number sentence shows the check?' (key 32 × 1/4 = 8). Keep story-match and role subtypes unchanged.

widgets.component: Cut the bars: cut whole bars into equal pieces, count groups, type the quotient
widgets.root: This is the lesson's manipulable model: pieces per bar must line up with the divisor, graded traps for multiplied, flipped, counted pieces not groups. Sampled 12 seeds: 2-5 wholes ÷ 1/q with q ≤ 6.

widgets.component: Why is the answer bigger than 6? / If each section were 1/2 yard instead, how many sections?
widgets.root: These are connect.check items 2 and 3 lifted without the scenario (6 yards of crime-scene tape cut into 1/3-yard sections) and without its tape-diagram figure, so 'the answer' and 'sections' refer to nothing on the page and 5.3 cannot be solved.
widgets.replacement: In scripts/lib/practice-studio-config.mjs buildSections (mastery = convert(connect) + exit + mastery) prefix connect.check items with cfg.connect.scenario and carry cfg.connect.diagram as item.viz. Or rewrite: 5.2 'A detective cuts 6 yards of tape into sections that are each 1/3 yard, so 6 ÷ 1/3 = 18 sections. Why is 18 bigger than 6?' and 5.3 'A detective cuts 6 yards of tape into sections that are each 1/2 yard. How many sections?' (key 12) with the tape diagram.

widgets.component: Climb the ladder: numeric L2; L4 missing dividend/divisor, 'dividing always makes smaller' replies, check-by-multiplying choices
widgets.root: Checked 59 seeds of L4: answers are exact, replies to 'dividing always makes smaller' name the pieces-fit idea, and the check-by-multiplying choice is 2/3 ÷ 2 = 1/3 → 1/3 × 2.

widgets.component: Sound-studio multi-step missions, quotient × divisor check table, who-is-right, situation choice
widgets.root: Recomputed every key (4 kits from 18 pieces, 1/4 hour, table 12/6, 32/4, 1/6/1/3, 1/6/5/6, 20 feet, 10 ÷ 1/2, 12 × 4 check); the check table (quotient × divisor) is numeric so it grades by value.

widgets.component: Cut the bars with a fraction ÷ whole number, then pick the division sentence the model shows
widgets.root: L3/L4 build the dividend as w·q+p over q with w = 1-2, so many draws are mixed numbers ('A 2 1/2-foot board is shared equally by 3', 1 1/4 ÷ 3); mixed numbers are 6-2 and 6-10 content and the objective names only whole numbers and unit fractions.
widgets.replacement: In assets/studio-act/barcut.js accept params.maxWhole and set w = 0 when it is 0, then author these two activities with {"mode":"fracByWhole","maxWhole":0}. L3 keeps non-unit numerators (3/4 ÷ 3), L4 keeps the reverse 'pick the division sentence'.

widgets.root: Each story maps to one expression; the pairs deliberately mix both meanings.

widgets.component: Explain why dividing by 1/2 gives more than dividing by 2; create your own problem
widgets.root: Completion needs only 40 characters and the learner's own ticks on a rubric; the model answer appears in full as soon as the box is filled, so nothing checks the mathematics.
widgets.replacement: Keep the prompt, but require two structured parts before the model answer opens: (1) a number-sentence box accepted only if it parses to a division with the story's numbers, (2) a one-line choice 'my answer is bigger / smaller than the starting amount because ...' graded by choosing from three reasons; show the model answer after both.

formulaOrder.formula: dividing by a fraction = multiplying by its reciprocal (keep-change-flip)
